articles.title: HOLDING THE DOOR FOR AGENTS
articles.summary: Developers are handing routine deployment work to AI agents. Cloud host Fly.io says at least 55% of its deployments now come from agents. Users want agents to work without dashboard interruptions, so Fly.io provides auth.md instructions for signup with human email confirmation and a code. The resulting credentials expire after 24 hours and exclude billing or organization membership changes. Agents can also request fixed credit purchases that a human approves in Stripe's Link app after reading the agent's stated reason.

articles.title: YOUR NEXT CUSTOMER WILL SEND AN AGENT
articles.summary: Shopping has had four mega waves in 110 years. Self-service arrived in 1916, the card in 1950, the internet in 1994, and the phone in 2007. Each one took one more person or step out of the purchase. The next wave will take out the customer.

articles.title: THE BAR TO GET FUNDED IS FAR HIGHER THAN MOST FOUNDERS REALIZE: 900% MEDIAN GROWTH UNDER $10M, 115% AT $100M+, AND $655K IN REVENUE PER EMPLOYEE
articles.summary: Tripling from $3M to $9M ARR used to be a sure path to a term sheet. Now it trails the 900% median growth of the sub-$10M AI companies that top growth funds are backing, and those same companies get funded with only 55% gross margins and 105% net revenue retention. About 10% of VCs still back a triple-triple-double plan, so founders growing 2 to 3x should build a much longer investor list and price their round modestly.

articles.title: 99 FOR FOUNDERS IS BACK
articles.summary: Smart people learn from others, often, and as broadly and as deeply as they can. This post is part of a series of lessons for founders and investors collected from founders. The advice covers fundraising, product, governance, competition, operations, exiting, and much more. Each piece of advice was chosen to help founders think in a way they may not have thought in before.

articles.title: WHERE AI ANSWERS GET THEIR SOURCES: 4,912 ANSWERS ACROSS SIX SOFTWARE CATEGORIES
articles.summary: Software buyers now ask AI assistants to compare tools like auth providers and Postgres hosting. Notra tested buyer questions across software categories to compare which sources assistants cite. ChatGPT never cited Reddit or YouTube within the reports' top-ten domain comparisons, while Google's AI Overviews often did. The cited pages differ by engine, so teams should check which comparison pages show up for their buyers' questions. Brands named in at least half the answers had their own sites cited in a median 12% of answers.

articles.title: AGENTS CAN NOW MANAGE AI GATEWAY THROUGH VERCEL MCP
articles.summary: Vercel's AI Gateway now lets AI agents connected through Vercel MCP set routing rules and configure spending budgets under existing team permissions. Agents can also create reusable virtual model IDs so teams can swap underlying models later without updating clients or redeploying.

articles.title: VERCEL STANDARD BUILDS
articles.summary: Existing Pro teams no longer get an included Standard build slot. Every standard build now bills at $0.014 per minute under usage-based Pro billing. Teams with heavy build pipelines should check their projected minutes before it shows up on the invoice.

articles.title: FRAMER AUTOMATIONS, CONNECTORS, AND SLACK AGENT
articles.summary: Framer sites can now run automated workflows on a schedule or on project events, like an SEO audit on publish or lead enrichment on a form submission. New connectors pull in Slack, Notion, and Ahrefs, and a @Framer Slack app handles site edits and analytics without opening the dashboard.

articles.title: WHY 2027 IS THE YEAR OF USER
articles.summary: Everything that only deals with 'things' and not with 'people' is quickly losing value. AI will soon solve all tasks with verifiable rewards. They can build almost anything very easily. The new metrics that still work are how many resources you have that other people cannot get, and how much your work affects people. Both require real people to spend time or money, as nobody can generate them from nothing.

articles.title: STARTUPS ARE PICKING NAMES THAT CAN WORK EVEN IF THE ORIGINAL BUSINESS MODEL DOESN'T
articles.summary: Recently funded startups are favoring names that are distinctive but vague, like Also, Sunday, or Flapping Airplanes, so they can pivot without a rebrand. Many companies make one or two major pivots within seven or eight years.

articles.title: THE FALL FUNDRAISING WINDOW IS NOW CLOSED
articles.summary: Fundraising processes launched after Thanksgiving run into the December holiday break. Pushing to close before year-end for founders who already hold a signed term sheet. Founders with soft-circled angels and no lead can close those commitments now so they do not lose them. Founders without real investor traction should consider pausing to improve the business and restart in January. Casual intro calls in December can still build relationships for January.
